brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.

requirements.evidence: 3 full hex-bin-full bins: bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0 in a straight row on 3 full bases; soil filled in each
507 x 89 x 384 mm single-storey straight row of 3 cells, seen with props in look view
requirements.requirement: Suits a kitchen windowsill (narrow, low, sill-sized row)

requirements.evidence: prop:1 basil-young, prop:2 parsley-young, prop:3 chives-young, one per bin, all in soil; check_build ok, meshClash clear, no prop warnings

finish.summary: 3-cell straight planter row with basil, parsley and chives, each in soil in its own bin. Verified clear with herbs visible.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A sunny trio for your sill — I'll build the planter.
